sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

Limited data indicate that trace amounts of iron dextran are excreted into breastmilk. No information is available on the clinical use of iron dextran during breastfeeding. However, intravenous iron dextran has been used in preterm infants for anemia of prematurity and would not be expected to cause any adverse effects in breastfed infants. An alternate intravenous drug with more published data available may be preferred.
For additional information on iron use during breastfeeding, see the monograph on Iron Salts.
